positions.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Beausoleil Smith supports a Renters' Bill of Rights to keep Portlanders in their homes.
positions.excerpt: A Renters’ Bill of Rights will keep Portlanders in their homes

positions.statement: Beausoleil Smith's pamphlet statement prioritizes fixing potholes and expanding pedestrian and cyclist infrastructure with union jobs.
positions.excerpt: fixing potholes, expanding pedestrian & cyclist infrastructure with union jobs

positions.statement: In his pamphlet statement, Beausoleil Smith says he will push for safe school routes, expanding Portland Street Response and faster emergency response times.
positions.excerpt: I’ll fight for safe school routes, Expanding Portland Street Response, and faster emergency response times.

positions.statement: Beausoleil Smith's pamphlet statement lists protecting trans and immigrant neighbors and holding ICE accountable.
positions.excerpt: Protecting our Trans and Immigrant Neighbors and Holding ICE Accountable.

positions.statement: In his pamphlet statement, Beausoleil Smith says he supports a four-year ban on AI data centers.

positions.statement: In his pamphlet statement, Beausoleil Smith says he opposes what he describes as genocide in Gaza.

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 12 District 4 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form (linked from portland.gov 2026 city candidates page); (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the two articles that profile every District 4 candidate: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 4 council race' (2026-10-07) and Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 4' (2026-09-11). Multi-winner race: OPB states three District 4 seats are on the ballot. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report.
